transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess what brings me in is, sometimes after work, or after a tense dinner, I’ll start eating and it kind of feels like the part of me that’s supposed to decide things just… shuts off. Like I can see myself reaching for more, and I know I probably should stop, but in the moment I can’t really make myself. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Can you tell me more about that feeling when you say the part of you that decides things shuts off? Does it feel like you're unable to control what or how much you're eating in those moments?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the best way to put it. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because it’s not like I’m trying to be reckless or anything, but in those moments it does feel like I’m not really in charge.

Like after work, or if dinner’s been tense, I’ll start eating and then… I can sort of see myself going back for more, and I know I should stop, or I tell myself, “Okay, that’s enough,” but it doesn’t really land. It’s like the deciding part of my brain just goes quiet for a while. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me how often this tends to happen? Like, do you find yourself having these kinds of eating episodes regularly, maybe even multiple times a week?

Um… yeah, I guess it is regular. I don’t think it’s every day or anything, but for the last few months it’s been… most weeks, I’d say, where I have at least one night where it feels out of control.

And then afterward I usually feel like I need to fix it somehow. I’m a little embarrassed to say that. Sometimes I’ll make myself throw up, or I’ll take laxatives, or I’ll skip meals the next day. Other times I’ll kind of force myself to go on a really long walk, like I’m trying to undo it. I know that probably doesn’t sound great.

Can you tell me more about the times when you feel like you're not in charge while eating—does it feel like you’re completely unable to control how much you eat during those episodes, even if you want to stop?

Yeah… I mean, “completely” feels like a strong word, but… in the moment it kind of does feel that way.

Some nights, usually after work or if dinner was tense, I’ll start eating and then it’s like the part of me that’s supposed to decide what I’m doing just sort of shuts off. I can see myself getting more food, and I know I want to stop—or I think, “You should stop now”—but I can’t really make myself do it right then. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s fair. I don’t like saying I “can’t” stop, because it makes me sound like I’m just not trying, but in those moments it really does feel like that.

Usually it’s after work, or if dinner felt tense, and I’ll start eating and then I can almost watch myself reaching for more. I’ll think, “Okay, stop now,” but it’s like the part of me that makes that decision just… shuts off for a bit. Does that make sense?
During these episodes, do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s basically what brought me in.

Some nights after work, or if dinner has been tense, I’ll start eating and it’s like the decision-making part of me just sort of shuts off. I can see myself reaching for more food, and I’m thinking I should stop, but in that moment I can’t really make myself stop. Does that answer what you mean?
Once you start eating during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you continue to eat, even if you want to?

Yeah… I think that’s the best way to put it. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just out of control all the time, because it’s not like that, but on those nights—after work, or if dinner was kind of tense—I’ll start eating and then it feels like the decision-making part of me just switches off.

I can sort of see myself going back for more food, and I’m thinking I should stop, but I can’t seem to make myself stop right then. I guess that’s what worried me enough to come in.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’re not in control of how much you’re eating, like you’re not able to stop even though you want to?

Yes… yeah, that’s basically it. I feel embarrassed saying it that way, because it sounds dramatic, but some nights after work, or if dinner was tense, I’ll start eating and it’s like the part of me that decides to stop just kind of shuts off.

I can see myself reaching for more, and I’m thinking, “You should stop now,” but I don’t really feel able to make myself stop in that moment. That’s really what made me think I should talk to someone.
Do these episodes of feeling out of control while eating happen mainly in response to specific emotional triggers, like feeling stressed after work or during tense situations?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. It’s not every time I’m upset or anything, but it does seem to happen more on nights after work, or if dinner has been tense.

That’s kind of what brought me in, honestly. I’ll start eating and then it feels like the part of me that’s supposed to decide, “Okay, stop now,” just shuts off. I can see myself reaching for more food, and I know I don’t really want to keep going, but in the moment I can’t seem to make myself stop. Does that make sense?

Do these episodes of feeling out of control while eating usually happen when you're alone, and do they tend to be followed by behaviors like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or restricting food the next day?

Mostly when I’m alone, yeah… usually after everyone’s gone to bed. I don’t really like admitting this, but there have been times where I’ve gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up afterward.

And… sometimes I’ve taken laxatives too. I kind of tell myself in the moment that I’m just trying to “undo the damage,” which I know probably doesn’t sound good. Afterward I feel really embarrassed, and sometimes shaky. I’m sorry—this is hard to say out loud.
Do these episodes bother you a lot, or do they affect your daily life—like how you feel about yourself, your relationships, or how you function at work?

It does bother me, yeah… I mean, I’m still getting to work and doing my cashier shifts. I’m not, like, falling apart or anything. I handle what I need to handle.

But it’s started to affect things a bit. I’ll avoid family meals sometimes afterward, or I’ll be there but kind of distracted, because I’m thinking about what I ate or worrying about what I’m going to do to make up for it. I don’t know if that counts as affecting daily life, but… it doesn’t feel great.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're just chewing and swallowing without really thinking about it, like your eating is happening on its own without you fully deciding to do it?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if I’d say I’m completely not thinking, but it feels like the part of me that’s supposed to make decisions just sort of shuts off.

Like I can see myself reaching for more food, and I know I should stop, or that I don’t really want to keep going, but I just… don’t stop. It’s usually on those nights after work or when dinner’s been tense. I’m aware of it happening, which almost makes it worse, but I don’t feel like I’m fully in control. Does that answer what you mean?

Have these episodes or the behaviors that follow, like making yourself vomit or skipping meals, caused you a lot of distress or made it harder for you to function in your relationships, at work, or in other parts of your life?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s made me unable to function or anything. I’m still going to work, still doing my cashier shifts, still taking care of what I’m supposed to.

But it does get in the way some. Like after it happens, I’ll avoid family meals sometimes, or I’ll sit there but I’m not really present because I’m thinking about what I ate or what I’m going to do to make up for it. It’s embarrassing to admit, but it does cause me stress. I don’t know if that’s “a lot,” but… it’s definitely there.

Do you ever feel like you’re almost on autopilot while eating during these episodes, where you’re not really tasting the food or thinking about what you’re doing—it just kind of happens without you fully deciding to do it?

Yeah… that’s pretty close to what it feels like. Not every single time, but some nights after work, or if dinner’s been tense, I’ll start eating and it’s like the decision-making part of me just kind of shuts off.

I can see myself reaching for more food, and part of me is thinking, “You should stop,” but I just… don’t. I’m not trying to make it sound dramatic, but it does feel like I’m not fully deciding anymore. Does that make sense?
While you're eating during these episodes, do you ever feel detached from yourself or like you're watching yourself do it without really being in control?

Yeah… I think so, at least somewhat. I don’t want to overstate it, like I’m completely outside my body or anything, but there are times where I’m eating and it’s like I’m watching myself keep going.

I can see myself reaching for more food, and I know I should stop, but that part of me that makes the decision just feels like it shuts off. It’s usually after work or if dinner’s been tense. I’m there, but I don’t feel fully in control, if that makes sense.

During these episodes, do you ever feel completely detached from yourself, like you're not really present in your body or that you're watching yourself act without being able to control what's happening?

Not completely detached, no… I don’t think I’d say it that strongly. I’m still aware of what I’m doing.

But what brought me in is that some nights, like after work or after a tense dinner, I’ll start eating and it’s like the part of me that makes decisions just shuts off. I can see myself reaching for more food, and I know I should stop, but I can’t seem to make myself stop in that moment.

I don’t know if that counts as what you mean, but that’s what it feels like.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating even if you really want to, like it's physically impossible to stop once you've started?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say physically impossible exactly, but in the moment it really does feel like I can’t stop.

What brought me in is that some nights after work, or after a tense dinner, I’ll start eating and it’s like the decision-making part of me just… shuts off. I can see myself reaching for more food, and I’m thinking I should stop, I really want to stop, but I can’t seem to make myself do it right then. If that makes sense.
